title: Descent of filtered chain maps to coherent quotient pages
statement: Let $C$ be abelian [def-sp-abelian], $K,K\prime$ be integer-indexed cochain complexes, and $F,F\prime$ decreasing filtrations by subcomplexes [def-sp-filtration]. Let $E,E\prime$ be cohomological spectral sequences beginning at page one [def-sp-spectral-sequence], with concrete quotient identifications $e,e\prime$ and quotient coherence [def-weil-pbc-filtered-quotient-coherence]. Suppose a chain map $b:K\to K\prime$ has restrictions to every filtration step, commuting with the step inclusions. Then there exists a spectral-sequence morphism $N:E\to E\prime$ whose components send every graded cycle representative of $x$ to that of $bx$. Precisely, for any test object $A$, degree $(p,q)$, positive page $r$, representatives $x:A\to F^pK^{p+q}$ and $y:A\to F\prime{}^pK\prime{}^{p+q}$ with $xb=y$ after step inclusions, and graded cycles $z,z\prime$ projecting from $x,y$, one has $z\pi_r e_r^{-1}N_r=z\prime\pi\prime_r e\prime_r{}^{-1}$. No finiteness, projectivity, CE resolution or first-page cohomology identification is assumed.

proof.text: Restrict b to the steps, descend through the graded projections, restrict to the cycle image subobjects and boundary image subobjects, and apply cokernel.map. The chain-map equation preserves the pullbacks defining cycles and the differential images defining boundaries. This gives each quotient component and its representative equation.

Conjugate the quotient components by the supplied e. On the epimorphic representative covers, the differential equations in quotient coherence and b.comm give the chain-map equation for each page; cancel the representative epimorphisms.

Use the epic cover of page cycles by successor cycles. Precompose each successor square with that cover and the homology projection. The two successor equations of quotient coherence reduce the square to the already established successor quotient representative equation. Cancel the composite epimorphism and assemble the page chain maps into N.
